message.content:
If \(M=0\), then \(\alpha=\beta=0\), giving \(100=0\), impossible. So \(M>0\).

Write
\[
\alpha=Me^{i\theta},\qquad \beta=Me^{i\phi}.
\]
Let
\[
t=\frac{\theta+\phi}{2},\qquad c=\cos\left(\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}\right),\qquad z=e^{it}.
\]
Then
\[
\alpha+\beta=2Mc\,z,\qquad \alpha\beta=M^2z^2.
\]
The condition becomes
\[
M^2z^2+2Mc\,z+100=0.
\]
Solving for \(c\),
\[
c=-\frac12\left(Mz+\frac{100}{M}z^{-1}\right).
\]
Since \(c\) is real and \(z=e^{it}\),
\[
Mz+\frac{100}{M}z^{-1}
=\left(M+\frac{100}{M}\right)\cos t+i\left(M-\frac{100}{M}\right)\sin t.
\]
Thus
\[
\left(M-\frac{100}{M}\right)\sin t=0.
\]

If \(M\neq 10\), then \(\sin t=0\), so \(z=\pm1\) and
\[
|c|=\frac12\left(M+\frac{100}{M}\right)\ge 10>1,
\]
impossible because \(c=\cos(\cdot)\in[-1,1]\). Hence \(M=10\).

Finally, \(M=10\) is attainable: \(\alpha=10,\ \beta=-10\) gives
\[
\alpha\beta+\alpha+\beta+100=-100+0+100=0.
\]

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
